name: Parachi
catalog_citation: Efimov, V. A. 1999. 'Parachi jazyk' [Парачи язык]. In: V. S. Rastorgueva (ed.), Jazyki mira: Iranskie jazyki. II. Severo-zapadnye iranskie jazyki, pp. 257-275. Moskva: Indrik.
catalog_locator: sec. 2.1.2, p. 260 (PDF p. 260 of the iling-ran.ru volume scan; page image the copy we hold; text layer)
catalog_quote: 2.1.2. Ударение динамическое, свободное (разноместное), подвижное. В двусложных словах падает либо на первый, либо на второй от начала слова слог. В многосложных словах, численно уступающих одно- и двусложным, тяготеет к концу слова: wåšená 'петух', r‘awaté 'расческа', kasångáṇḍ 'одеяло'. В формах мн. числа существительных ударение, как правило, падает на формант; у имен с формантом -ån последний в одних случаях — ударный: pošấn 'сыновья', в других — безударный: gúšån 'уши'. В формах посессивного и отложительного падежа существительных ударение, как правило, падает на падежные показатели ... В косвенных падежах личных местоимений, представляющих собой двусложные или многосложные слова, ударение всегда падает на конечный слог. В формах аориста, образуемых от презентной основы, ударение может быть либо на основе (корне): jána 3 л. ед. ч. от jan- 'бить', bára 3 л. ед. ч. от bar- 'нести' ..…

new_statements.translation: 2.1.2. Stress is dynamic, free (not bound to a position), and mobile. In disyllabic words it falls either on the first or on the second syllable from the beginning of the word. In polysyllabic words, which are fewer than mono- and disyllables, it gravitates toward the end of the word: wåšená 'rooster', r‘awaté 'comb', kasångáṇḍ 'blanket'. In noun plural forms stress as a rule falls on the formant; with nouns taking the formant -ån the latter is in some cases stressed: pošấn 'sons', in others unstressed: gúšån 'ears'. In the possessive and ablative case forms of nouns stress as a rule falls on the case markers [...] In the oblique cases of personal pronouns [...] stress always falls on the final syllable.

В формах посессивного и отложительного падежа.. падает на падежные по…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Free (lexically/morphologically determined) dynamic stress with a statistical pull toward the word end: disyllables may be initial- or final-stressed; longer words are mostly final-stressed; inflectional suffixes (plural, possessive, ablative) usually attract stress, but plural -ån is stressed with some nouns and unstressed with others (Trofimov 2021 traces this to Proto-Iranian oxytone vs barytone stems); aorist verb forms are either stem-stressed or ending-stressed by lexeme (an inherited contrast, now largely levelled by analogy). Morgenstierne 1929: 21 adds that word stress is phonetically weak and varies with sentence stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Two-component (periphrastic) verb forms carry main stress on the lexical component and secondary stress on the auxiliary (r‘izō̃́ (h)ȍst 'he lay'); in negated verbs main stress is on the negative na-, secondary on the syllable stressed in the affirmative (ná-uzå̏(w)ō 'he did not stay').
new_statements.exceptions: Unstressed: definite articles ē, ō and indefinite žu, enclitic pronouns (γós-om 'my house'), prepositions and postpositions, the predicative copula (unless negated), modal particle -e/-y and particles te, xo/xu. Aorist stem-stress vs ending-stress opposition 'to a considerable degree neutralized' by analogical levelling.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level description with citation forms carrying accent marks throughout the sketch; Morgenstierne 1929 sec. 23 explicitly notes word stress 'is not very marked, and varies a good deal according to sentence stress', i.e. phrase prosody can override.
new_statements.identity_note: Efimov 1999 describes Parachi as a whole (his own 1960s-70s fieldwork, Shutul/Ghochulan/Pachaghan varieties) = Glottolog para1299. Morgenstierne 1929 is based mainly on Shutul and Nijrau speakers; same language. The Efimov 1999 wording is essentially identical to Efimov 2009: 29 as quoted verbatim by Trofimov 2022: 226, so the 2009 grammar would not change the reading.

sources.note: Sec. 2.1.2 p. 260: stress dynamic, free (raznomestnoe), mobile; in disyllables on either 1st or 2nd syllable; in polysyllables (rarer) gravitates to the end of the word (wåšená, r'awaté, kasångáṇḍ); plural formant usually stressed (-ån stressed in some nouns, unstressed in others); possessive/ablative case markers stressed; oblique personal pronouns always final-stressed; aorist forms stem- or ending-stressed (inherited Old Iranian present-stem accent contrast, now largely levelled); compound verb forms have main + secondary stress; negation takes main stress; articles, enclitic pronouns, adp…

sources.citation: Trofimov, A. A. 2022. 'Udarenie v jazykax parachi i ormuri v svjazi s afganskim i ego znachenie dlja iranskoj rekonstrukcii' [The accent in Parachi and Ormuri compared to Pashto and its significance for the reconstruction of Proto-Iranian]. Journal of Language Relationship / Voprosy jazykovogo rodstva 20(3-4): 222-252.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 226 quotes Efimov 2009: 29 verbatim: 'Ударение в парачи динамическое, свободное (разноместное), подвижное. В двусложных словах падает либо на первый, либо на второй от начала слова слог. В многосложных словах.. ударение тяготеет к концу слова: wåšená, rhawaṭé, kasångáṇḍ'; notes that basic disyllabic oxytone stems in Parachi usually lost original oxytonesis (Efimov 1985: 49-50); rest is diachronic comparison of Parachi/Ormuri/Pashto reflexes of Proto-Iranian barytona/oxytona.

sources.citation: Trofimov, A. A. 2021. 'Udarenie mnozhestvennogo chisla imen s pokazatelem -ån v parachi i ego svjaz' s prairanskoj akcentuaciej' [Stress position of nominal plurals in -ån in Parachi and its connection with Proto-Iranian accent]. Journal of Language Relationship 19(3-4): 210-231.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Plural -ån is stressed with some nouns (pošấn 'sons') and unstressed with others (gúšån 'ears'); argues inherited barytone stems keep stem stress and oxytone stems take ending stress in the plural (9 vs 10 inherited items), while singulars have lost the Proto-Iranian distinction; quotes Efimov 1997: 479-480 at length.

sources.note: Sec. 23 'Stress', p. 21: 'Word stress is not very marked, and varies a good deal according to sentence stress. Cf. 44.' Secs. 44-45 (pp. 30-32) reconstruct the pre-Parachi accent (quantity-based, Meillet-Gauthiot type: long penult stressed, etc.) from vowel elisions; footnote in verb section: 'The accent is not fixed, 'merem, me'rem etc. are frequently heard.' No synchronic placement rule beyond this.
